title: Paracetamol: general adult uses
text: Paracetamol is a common painkiller used to relieve aches, pain and high temperature (fever) in adults. It is available in forms such as tablets, capsules, liquid and suppositories. People with liver or kidney problems, or a prior allergic reaction to paracetamol, should seek pharmacist or medical advice before use. Many cold and flu remedies also contain paracetamol, so labels must be checked to avoid accidental excess intake. General UK reference only; not a personal treatment or dose instruction.

title: Paracetamol: possible side effects and warnings
text: Paracetamol rarely causes side effects when taken as directed on the leaflet. Serious reactions are uncommon but can include severe allergic swelling or breathing difficulty, liver injury, or blood disorders causing unusual bruising or infections. Urgent medical attention is required for suspected excess intake or severe warning signs rather than waiting for an assistant response. This summary is not a complete side-effect list or a clinical diagnosis; consult the product leaflet and a qualified healthcare professional.

title: Metformin: general uses in type 2 diabetes
text: Metformin is a prescription medicine mainly used to treat type 2 diabetes by helping to lower blood glucose levels and improve how the body responds to insulin. It may also be prescribed for other clinician-managed conditions. Suitability and monitoring depend on kidney function, other health conditions and concurrent medicines. A doctor or pharmacist must guide any prescription decisions. This educational summary does not recommend starting, stopping, substituting or adjusting a prescription.

title: Metformin: possible side effects and risks
text: Common possible side effects of metformin include nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, stomach ache, loss of appetite and a metallic taste. Long-term or susceptible users may develop vitamin B12 deficiency, though not everyone is affected. Rare but serious risks include lactic acidosis and severe allergic reactions; severe vomiting, deep rapid breathing, or extreme weakness require urgent medical care. Consult a pharmacist or doctor for persistent symptoms. This summary is not a complete monograph.

title: Cetirizine: general allergy uses
text: Cetirizine is an antihistamine medicine used to relieve allergy symptoms such as hay fever, conjunctivitis, eczema itch, hives (urticaria) and reactions to insect bites or stings. It blocks histamine effects to reduce sneezing, itching and watery eyes. People with severe kidney impairment, epilepsy or predisposition to urinary retention should check suitability with a pharmacist or doctor before use. This is general educational information, not a personal treatment recommendation.

title: Cetirizine: possible side effects and drowsiness caution
text: Although cetirizine is classed as a non-drowsy or less-drowsy antihistamine, it can still cause sleepiness and fatigue in some people. Other possible common side effects include headache, dry mouth, feeling sick, dizziness, diarrhoea and sore throat. Users should not drive, cycle or operate machinery if affected by drowsiness or dizziness. Severe allergic reactions require urgent medical care. Check the product leaflet and ask a pharmacist if side effects persist.

title: Amoxicillin: general bacterial infection uses
text: Amoxicillin is a prescription penicillin antibiotic used to treat certain bacterial infections, such as chest infections, ear infections, dental abscesses and urinary tract infections. Like all antibiotics, it does not work for viral infections such as colds or flu. It is unsuitable for anyone with a history of penicillin allergy. Only a qualified clinician can determine whether an antibiotic is appropriate; this summary does not provide prescribing or dosing instructions.

title: Amoxicillin: possible side effects and allergy warnings
text: Common possible side effects of amoxicillin include feeling sick (nausea), diarrhoea and mild skin rashes. Rare but serious side effects include severe watery or bloody diarrhoea, liver inflammation (yellowing skin or eyes), and severe immediate or delayed allergic reactions (anaphylaxis or blistering skin rash). Breathing difficulty, facial or throat swelling, or severe rash require urgent medical help. Consult a doctor or pharmacist if side effects are severe or persistent.

title: Ibuprofen: general NSAID uses and precautions
text: Ibuprofen is a non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID) used to relieve pain, fever and inflammation in conditions such as toothache, headache, period pain, sprains and arthritis. It is not suitable for everyone; people with stomach ulcers, asthma worsened by NSAIDs, severe heart, kidney or liver disease, or pregnancy should seek professional medical or pharmacist advice before use. General educational overview only; not an individual treatment or dose recommendation.

title: Ibuprofen: possible side effects and gastrointestinal risks
text: Common possible side effects of oral ibuprofen include indigestion, heartburn, stomach pain, nausea, headache and dizziness. Serious risks include stomach ulceration or gastrointestinal bleeding (indicated by black tarry stools or vomiting blood), kidney impairment, severe allergic reactions or worsened asthma wheezing. Urgent medical care is required for signs of bleeding, chest pain or breathing difficulty. Consult a pharmacist or doctor regarding drug interactions and personal suitability.

title: Atorvastatin: general cholesterol and cardiovascular uses
text: Atorvastatin is a prescription statin medicine used to lower blood cholesterol and reduce the risk of cardiovascular events such as heart attack and stroke. It is prescribed alongside lifestyle measures under medical supervision. Suitability depends on liver health, muscle history, pregnancy status and interacting medicines or grapefruit juice. A doctor or pharmacist must advise on prescription management. This summary does not recommend starting, stopping or changing treatment.

title: Atorvastatin: possible side effects and muscle warnings
text: Common possible side effects of atorvastatin include indigestion, headache, nausea, diarrhoea or constipation, cold-like symptoms and mild joint or muscle ache. Unexplained muscle pain, tenderness or weakness can rarely signal serious muscle breakdown (rhabdomyolysis) and requires prompt medical evaluation. Other rare serious risks include liver problems (yellowing skin or eyes) and severe allergic reactions. Always consult a doctor or pharmacist if unexplained muscle symptoms or side effects occur.

title: Losartan: general blood pressure and kidney protection uses
text: Losartan is a prescription angiotensin receptor blocker (ARB) used to treat high blood pressure (hypertension), protect kidney function in people with hypertension and type 2 diabetes, and manage heart failure. It relaxes blood vessels to lower blood pressure. Losartan is contraindicated in pregnancy and requires medical monitoring of kidney function and blood potassium. A clinician must direct its use; this summary does not provide dosing or treatment-change advice.

title: Losartan: possible side effects and monitoring cautions
text: Common possible side effects of losartan include dizziness or lightheadedness (especially when standing up), fatigue, low blood pressure and raised blood potassium levels. Rare serious risks include kidney impairment, liver inflammation, and severe allergic swelling of the face, lips, tongue or throat (angioedema). Urgent medical help is needed for facial or throat swelling or breathing difficulty. Consult a doctor or pharmacist before combining losartan with other medicines.

title: Omeprazole: general stomach acid and reflux uses
text: Omeprazole is a proton pump inhibitor (PPI) that reduces the amount of acid produced by the stomach. It is used for indigestion, heartburn, acid reflux, gastro-oesophageal reflux disease (GORD), and preventing or treating stomach ulcers. Persistent symptoms, difficulty swallowing, unexplained weight loss or vomiting require medical assessment rather than prolonged self-treatment. This educational overview does not recommend an individual dose or treatment duration.

title: Omeprazole: possible side effects and long-term cautions
text: Common possible side effects of omeprazole include headache, stomach pain, nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, constipation and excess wind. Rare or longer-term risks include low magnesium levels, vitamin B12 deficiency, bone fractures with prolonged use, kidney inflammation, severe persistent watery diarrhoea, and sun-sensitive skin rashes. Urgent care is required for severe allergic reactions or yellowing skin. Discuss ongoing use or side effects with a pharmacist or doctor.

title: Pantoprazole: general acid reflux and ulcer uses
text: Pantoprazole is a proton pump inhibitor (PPI) that decreases stomach acid production. It is used to treat heartburn, acid reflux, gastro-oesophageal reflux disease (GORD), and stomach or duodenal ulcers, and to protect the stomach in patients taking certain anti-inflammatory medicines. Persistent or alarm symptoms such as difficulty swallowing or unintentional weight loss require medical evaluation. This is general reference information, not a personal dosing or substitution instruction.

title: Pantoprazole: possible side effects and safety warnings
text: Pantoprazole often causes no side effects, or mild uncommon effects such as headache, diarrhoea, nausea, abdominal discomfort, dizziness or dry mouth. Rare serious risks include severe allergic reactions, liver problems, kidney inflammation, joint pain with sun-triggered skin rash, severe persistent diarrhoea, and low magnesium or bone fractures during long-term therapy. Seek urgent medical attention for severe allergic swelling or breathing difficulty, and consult a clinician for persistent symptoms.

title: Azithromycin: general macrolide antibiotic uses
text: Azithromycin is a prescription macrolide antibiotic used to treat specific bacterial infections, including chest, sinus, ear and skin infections, as well as certain sexually transmitted infections. It does not treat viral infections such as colds or flu. Suitability depends on liver or kidney conditions, heart rhythm history (QT prolongation) and interacting medicines. Only a qualified clinician can prescribe it; this summary provides no dosing or substitution advice.

title: Azithromycin: possible side effects and heart rhythm cautions
text: Common possible side effects of azithromycin include nausea, diarrhoea, vomiting, stomach cramps, loss of appetite, headache and dizziness. Rare serious risks include fast or irregular heartbeat (palpitations or QT prolongation), severe allergic reactions, liver inflammation, severe watery diarrhoea, and serious skin reactions. Seek urgent medical help for chest palpitations, fainting, severe rash or breathing difficulty. Consult a pharmacist or doctor regarding indigestion-remedy timing and interactions.

title: Medicine storage: general child safety and product-specific temperature gap
text: General household medication safety includes keeping medicines in original child-resistant containers with safety caps closed and stored out of sight and reach of children. Product-specific storage temperatures, refrigeration rules and shelf-life limits for individual medicines are not covered by this general summary; check the manufacturer package leaflet or ask a pharmacist.
